time.desc: The highest judicial authority agreed to expedite the acceptance of a short video platform’s appeal against the “forced stripping or banning” law and arranged a date for oral arguments but did not immediately issue a temporary stop order.

Two senior members of the Legislature sent a letter to the main app store operator, requesting it to remove the short video app from the store before the legal cutoff to cooperate with the implementation

The leader-elect submitted a document to the highest judicial authority arguing that the mandatory divestment cutoff for the app should be suspended to allow the new government to find a solution through political negotiations.

The federal government submitted its opinion to the highest judicial body, objecting to the request for a stay of execution submitted by the leader-elect and advocating that the law should remain in force as scheduled

The highest judicial authority held an oral argument on the dispute over the ban of the short video platform. During the trial, the judges were generally more inclined to accept the "national security" reason and questioned the platform's claim of freedom of speech.

The current government has publicly stated that it will not proactively enforce relevant prohibition laws on the legal effective date, and will leave the actual enforcement to the incoming new government.

The highest judicial authority rejected the emergency stop application filed by the platform and users, allowing the "forced divestment or ban" law to take effect as scheduled (full reasons will be announced separately)

The short video platform experienced key service changes before and after local restrictions were implemented: it first stopped services in the country and was removed from major app stores. At the same time, the then leader announced that he would try to suspend the implementation of administrative measures after taking office.

The short video platform restored access to domestic users after the leader-elect publicly stated that he would use administrative measures to secure buffers for the platform and signaled that service providers would not be held accountable.
The new government signed an executive order to postpone the implementation of the ban on the short video platform by about two months to gain time for transactions and disposals.

The new government signed an executive order to promote the establishment of a sovereign investment fund and made it clear that this tool may be used to participate in the acquisition of the short video platform as an alternative solution path

After the regulatory authorities issued written guarantees against liability to app store operators, the short video platform resumed listing and downloading on major app stores, ending a download ban that lasted for several weeks.
A Northeast Asian country's data regulator confirmed that a chatbot company had shared user data with the parent company of the short video platform and initiated a formal inquiry process

Country A Leaders stated that the sale agreement for the short video platform is expected to be reached before the cutoff, and said that multiple buyers are actively participating in the negotiations.
The leader-elect made his first public statement in support of the short video platform's continued operation in the country at a rally and later met with the platform's CEO

For the first time, the platform invoked the freedom of speech clause to defend itself, saying that the authorities’ failure to ban other apps owned by foreign countries showed that the real target was content rather than data.
Leader-elect's nominee for attorney general publicly criticizes platform bans for widespread and troubling impact on free speech
During the oral argument, most judges expressed doubts about the platform’s claims and tended to support legislation based on national security considerations.
Platform X Parent Company Y Publicly refuses to break up or sell Platform X business

Thirteen, a subsidiary of billionaire Sixty-Three, officially submitted a proposal to acquire Platform X to Company Y, intending to migrate the application to the technology platform owned by Country A
Attorney-elect Leader A submitted a brief to Court D stating his "opposition to the ban on Platform X" and requesting that the ban be postponed to seek a political solution.

Leader A The government is in talks with Company O and an outside investor group to take over the operations of Platform X, with Company Y proposed to retain a minority stake and be controlled by Country A investors

Leader A publicly stated that it was negotiating with multiple parties for the acquisition of Platform X and would make a decision within 30 days, and named Entrepreneur E or Entrepreneur L E as potential buyers.
Leader A Designates Vice President Vice President V to be responsible for facilitating the potential sale of Platform X
